hero.title: Master’s in Electronics Engineering in Switzerland for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: A Master’s in Electronics Engineering in Switzerland is a good choice for students who are interested in semiconductor technology, microelectronics, integrated circuit design, embedded systems, sensors, communication devices and advanced electronic hardware. The Swiss technical universities offer research-oriented education with opportunities to explore the applications in robotics, medical technology, telecommunications and energy systems.

overview: A Master’s in Electronics Engineering in Switzerland is a good choice for students who are interested in semiconductor technology, microelectronics, integrated circuit design, embedded systems, sensors, communication devices and advanced electronic hardware. The Swiss technical universities offer research-oriented education with opportunities to explore the applications in robotics, medical technology, telecommunications and energy systems.
ETH Zurich and EPFL typically offer electronics-related programs of 2 years duration, with a total of 120 ECTS credits.

sections.title: Is it possible for Indian students to study electronics in English in Switzerland?
sections.lead: Yes. ETH Zurich offers the Electrical Engineering and Information Technology program in English. EPFL’s Electrical and Electronic Engineering program is also offered in English, with some optional courses in French language.

sections.title: What is the estimated cost for two years?
sections.lead: Planning estimates in this guide indicate that the cost of tuition and living expenses for a two-year program may be between ₹42.42 lakh and ₹69.70 lakh. Actual costs will vary depending on the university, accommodation and personal spending.

sections.title: Can I apply if I have a Bachelor’s in Electronics and Communication Engineering?
sections.lead: Maybe yeah. Related undergraduate degrees will be considered depending on the courses taken, the academic performance and the university’s requirements. Applicants must compare their transcripts with the programme’s academic requirements.

sections.title: Is it possible to work in Switzerland after graduation?
sections.lead: Maybe, but you don’t get a job automatically. Graduates are expected to obtain suitable employment and satisfy applicable Swiss immigration and work permit regulations. Job applications may be helped by relevant project experience, technical expertise and language skills.
